episodes.187290: An area of low pressure moved by to the south during the early morning hours of January 29th bringing a widespread inch and a half to two inches of rain. This resulted in some rivers rising into Minor Flood Stage and several streams overflowing their banks.

episodes.187737: Rain arrived into the area on January 27th ahead of a low pressure system and continued into the following day as the low progressed overhead. Around 1 to 2 inches of rain impacted portions of southeast Ohio, which had already experienced flooding with another system just days before. During the morning of the 28th, this new batch of rain initiated flooding along several creeks, streams, and rivers within the area. ||In addition to road closures, gages in Meigs and Washington Counties reported flooding along Duck Creek at Macksburg and below Whipple, the Little Muskingum River at Bloomfield, the Muskingum River at Beverly, and the Shade River near Chester. ||Both coverage and intensity of precipitation diminished during the afternoon and evening of the 28th, however moisture wrapping in behind the low continued to support light showers until later that night. Most creeks and streams lowered back into their banks the following morning, but some flooding persisted until the afternoon of the 29th.
episodes.187738: Rain entered into West Virginia on January 27th ahead of a low pressure system and continued into the following day as the low progressed overhead. Around 0.5 to 1.5 inches of rain fell across portions of the state which had already been impacted by another system just days before. In Pocahontas County, this new batch of rain initiated flooding along Knapp Creek on the morning of the 28th. The creek crested and then lowered back into its banks later that day.||Both coverage and intensity of precipitation diminished during the afternoon and evening hours of the 28th, but moisture wrapping in behind the low continued to support light showers and an eventual transition to snow later that night.
episodes.187925: A strong cold front on 01/28 brought heavy rain, which caused flooding on the Coquille River at Coquille.
episodes.188624: An upper level low pressure system passed up the Ohio River Valley on the 28th, drawing an associated occluded front across the central Appalachians.  Strong southerly windflow ahead of the front brought precipitable water values ranging from 1.0 to 1.1 inches over Greenbrier County, which is two standard deviations above normal per NWS climatology data.  This resulted in storm-total rainfall amounts across the county of between one and locally two inches, falling across soils that were not frozen, but were moderately moist from past rainfall events.  Runoff from this rainfall caused only minor localized flooding across the county.
episodes.188643: An upper level low pressure system passed up the Ohio River Valley on the 28th, drawing an associated occluded front across the central Appalachians.  Strong southerly windflow ahead of the front brought precipitable water values ranging from 1.2 to nearly 1.4 inches to over the Southside area of Virginia, which is between two and three standard deviations above normal per NWS climatology data.  This resulted in storm-total rainfall amounts across across Pittsylvania and Halifax Counties of between 1.75 and 2.25 inches, falling across soils that were not frozen, but were moderately moist from past rainfall events.  Runoff from this rainfall caused the Dan River at South Boston to rise above minor flood stage for the second time in January 2024, as well as localized flooding across portions of central Pittsylvania County.
episodes.188645: An upper level low pressure system passed up the Ohio River Valley on the 28th, drawing an associated occluded front across the central Appalachians.  Strong southerly windflow ahead of the front brought precipitable water values ranging from 1.1 to nearly 1.4 inches over northwest North Carolina, which is between 2 and 3 standard deviations above normal per NWS climatology data.  This resulted in storm-total rainfall amounts across middle-Dan River basin of between 2 and 3 inches, falling across soils that were not frozen, but were moderately moist from past rainfall events.  Runoff from this rainfall caused the Dan River at Wentworth to rise above minor flood stage for the second time in January 2024.
episodes.188781: A frontal system impacted the western Carolinas, bringing widespread showers and a few thunderstorms to upstate South Carolina. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Greenwood County.
episodes.189896: Minor flooding at Tualatin River at Farmington, Pudding River at Aurora, and Luckiamute River near Suver.

events.narrative: Public reported several large tree limbs blown down just north of Kirksey.

A National Weather Service storm survey team confirmed a brief EF-1 tornado, with|peak winds of 100 mph, Saturday evening in Northern Saluda County. The tornado|begin point and time was later adjusted slightly after new Sentinel satellite data|indicated the tornado touched down about 0.75 miles before the previously observed|damage. NDVI difference data & higher resolution visible imagery show an area of|trees down near the initial part of this track. The tornado then continued tracking to the |NE to near the intersection of Hunters Lane and Blue Spring Road producing|minor damage to two houses in addition to a large number of trees further down|Hunters Lane on both sides of the road where EF-1 damage was observed. The tornado|then moved northeast into an inaccessible wooded area behind homes on Blue Spring|Rd. The tornado turned slightly left crossing Blue Spring Rd in a NNE direction|producing EF-1 damage to another wooded area before dissipating in an open field|while approaching Hollywood Rd. The survey team estimated several hundred trees|were damaged along the path. Many of the trees were uprooted along with a few|trunks snapped. The damage to homes was mainly to the fascia board and missing|shingles.

After reviewing available data, a weak tornado has been determined to have briefly|touched down in far northern Saluda county on January 27. The tornado touched down|near Old Cherokee Trail before moving quickly northeast and causing limited tree damage|near Tostie Creek Road. The tornado then dissipated as it moved northeastward.
Runoff from the passage of a band of moderate to locally heavy rainfall resulted in water entering the basement of a home.
A tree was downed on Hwy 121 near Sulphur Springs Rd.  Time estimated.
The Accotink Creek at Woodburn Road/Strathmeade Springs crested at 252.14' in Minor Flood Stage. Both Woodburn Road and Prosperity Avenue were flooded by at least a foot of water.

Rock Creek at Sherrill Drive crested at 7.02' in Minor Flood Stage. Water reached several portions of the Valley Trail between Picnic Areas 7 and 10 in Rock Creek Park.	Water completely covered the Rolling Meadow Trailbridge.

Runoff from the passage of a band of heavy rainfall resulted in Chalk Level Road becoming flooded by several inches of water.  No damage was reported and the road was open to traffic after the water receded.
Little Bull Run at Artemus Road crested in Minor Flood Stage at 5.83 feet. Water from Little Bull Run overflowed on Artemus Road.
Difficult Run at Browns Mill Road/Wolf Trap crested at 196.08' in Minor Flood Stage. Water was overflowing Browns Mill Road.

The Harts Run Tunnel under the railroad tracks on Harts Run Road was flooded and impassable for a few hours due to runoff from prolonged rainfall collecting in the tunnel.  No damage was reported and the tunnel was open to traffic after the flooding receded.
The Route 63/Monroe Draft tunnel under the railroad was flooded and impassible due to runoff from heavy rain.  The tunnel was open to traffic after the water receded.  No damage was reported.

Tuckahoe Road at the railroad tunnel was flooded and impassible due to runoff from prolonged rainfall caused Dry Creek to flood out of its banks into the tunnel.  No damage was reported, and the tunnel was open to traffic after the water receded.
Reardon Road closed at Wrights Run due to high water.
Cedar Run near Aden crested at 11.45' in minor flood stage. Fleetwood Road flooded near Cedar Run. Water was over the banks, affecting agricultural land near Aden.
Kettle Run near Bristow Manor Golf Club crested at 6.84 feet in minor flood stage.
Beach Drive was closed due to flooding of Rock Creek.

In Huntersville, the gage on Knapp Creek exceeded its bankfull level of 9 feet on the morning of January 28th. The creek crested at 9.2 feet and then returned to its banks by late morning. Farmland, fields, and out buildings flooded along Knapp Creek and Browns Creek. Water came right up to but not over Route 39 near Huntersville.

A portion of Anthony Creek Trail at Blue Bend Loop Trail was flooded due to nearby Anthony Creek rising out of its banks.  No damage was reported, and the road was open to traffic after the water receded.

The Dan River at Wentworth, NC (WENN7) crested somewhere near a stage of 20.51 feet (18,600 cfs) at 5:00 pm EST on 1/10/24, rising above the minor flood stage of 19.0 feet. This is the second crest above flood stage at this gage during January 2024, and was around a 2-year ARI (50% AEP) per USGS StreamStats.  No damage was reported.

The gage at Macksburg on West Fork Duck Creek exceeded its bankfull level of 13 feet on the morning of January 28th, then rose to a crest around 14.4 feet overnight. The creek gradually lowered the morning of the 29th and fell back below bankfull early that afternoon. Flooding occurred on Main Street near the creek and in agricultural fields adjacent to the creek.
Heavy rain brought minor flooding to Tualatin River at Farmington.
Wolf Creek near Waterford exceeded its banks for a period of time and flooded adjacent farm fields.

The Little Muskingum River gage at Bloomfield exceeded its bankfull level of 16 feet in the early afternoon of January 28th. The river crested just over 20 feet overnight, then fell back below bankfull the following morning. Flooding occurred along Route 26 near the intersection with Route 260.

The Shade River gage near Chester exceeded its bankfull level of 16 feet on the morning of January 28th. The river crested just over 17 feet that afternoon, then gradually lowered below bankfull once again early the next morning. Flooding occurred along Scout Camp Creek Road and at the Sugar Run Creek Bridge. Fields adjacent to the river also flooded.

The Muskingum River gage at Beverly exceeded its minor flood stage of 29 feet the afternoon of January 28th. The river crested just over 30 feet during the evening, then fell back below flood stage early the next morning. Low areas, farmland, and a few homes along the river experienced flooding while the river was out of its banks.
State Route 554 was closed due to flooding from State Route 160 to North Walnut Street.
State Route 329 was closed in both directions due to flooding between State Route 144 and State Route 550.
Heavy rain caused minor flooding along the Luckiamute River near Suver.

The Coquille River at Coquille rose above minor flood stage of 21.0 ft at 28/1500 PST, and crested at minor flood stage at 21.15 ft at 28/1815 PST. The river dropped below minor flood stage at 29/0700 PST.

The River gauge on Opequon Creek Near Martinsburg reach minor flood stage with peak crest of 10.78 feet. At 10 feet, Douglas Grove Road begins to flood east of Martinsburg. A portion of Bowers Road is also flooded.
